accuracy_changes: Retired iex-finalscript: names such as finalScript, payload and decryptedScript prove neither decryption nor payload staging. The existing generic variable-eval capability remains visible.

AES stage execution consumers require the existing inline transform-to-eval link. The chunked helper consumer uses a generic IEX capability; the C2 consumer requires its upload evidence rather than a payload-named variable.
PowerShell decryptor-call and variable-eval co-occurrence is a notable capability; it does not establish shared data flow or malicious intent.

Decoded extraction coordinates now emit metadata/file/encoding::decoded-payload-layer and are excluded from the PE filename-mismatch observation. Real member filenames after a decoded archive remain eligible.
SETTINGS is matched as an eight-character length-prefixed UTF-16 resource name in .rsrc, avoiding dependency on decoded-string extraction. The complete resource-name observation is notable.
Remcos banner evidence, SETTINGS resource and RC4 implementation identify a configuration-analysis location without claiming decoded options or endpoints.
coverage_limits: The C2 address and enabled configuration options still require offline RC4 configuration reconstruction; the new rule does not emit plaintext configuration.
Headline descriptions distinguish API/resource co-occurrence from demonstrated process hollowing; static matches do not establish observed execution.
